en: The Second Book of Pairs (Dukanipāta), Chapter on Sandals (Upāhanavagga)
1. The Sandalwood-Boot Jātaka "Just as the sandals of a man, though made of wood,
are worn for the sake of comfort and ward off suffering;”
Scorched by the heat and oppressed by thirst on the dry land,
they devour the feet of that very man.
Even so is he who is of low birth and ignoble.
Therefore, having taken up both knowledge and learning,
he consumes that very thing there through his learning;
such a person is called ignoble, like one who wears ill-fitting sandals.
The Upāhana Jātaka is the first.
